work.title: FORM STUDY
work.subtitle: 桌面灯具概念设计说明书
work.framework: product: Design hypothesis / distinct native A4 document layout
work.scope: Fictional unpowered desk-lamp concept. No electrical design, safety certification, manufacturing specification, tested performance or production approval.

pages.title: Explain a form, not an electrical product.
pages.lead: FORM STUDY explores the visual character of an imagined unpowered desk-lamp object. It is a concept document, not a working lamp design or engineering instruction.
pages.body: The purpose is to make a design intention, alternative and evidence gap understandable. No wiring, power system, dimensions, test result or supplier is supplied.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: What can this concept document legitimately describe?

pages.title: Read the design argument.
pages.lead: The document moves from intention to context question, form, material appearance, alternatives, requirements and handoff. Keep the distinction between a sketch and a specification.
pages.body: The artwork shows a studio atmosphere. It cannot establish physical stability, lighting performance, electrical safety, manufacturing feasibility or actual user preference.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: Which claim would need a separate specialist source?

pages.title: Define the intended interaction.
pages.lead: Imagine an object that is easy to recognise as a focused desk companion. This is a visual intention, not a tested usability result or a claim about actual users.
pages.body: A real design brief would need a clear use context and appropriately obtained evidence. The template does not invent participant needs or research findings.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: What context would shape a real interaction question?

pages.title: Describe the form in ordinary language.
pages.lead: Discuss the relationship of base, stem and shade as a visual composition. Avoid supplying dimensions or implying that the depicted proportions have been engineered.
pages.body: A form can appear balanced without being physically stable. The distinction should remain visible in any caption or shared excerpt.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: Which visual adjective could be mistaken for a tested property?

pages.title: Treat materials as unverified appearances.
pages.lead: A surface may look metallic, matte or translucent in the illustration. Those appearances do not identify composition, durability or a safe application.
pages.body: No material sample, supplier declaration or test is supplied. Use appearance language and record the real source that would be needed before selection.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: What source would identify an actual material?

pages.title: Keep an alternative concept visible.
pages.lead: Compare a more compact visual form with a more open one as two imagined directions. Neither is a tested solution or a production-ready design.
pages.body: An alternative helps clarify the intended character. It does not prove superiority, cost advantage or suitability for a real setting.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: Which intention does the alternative test?

pages.title: Turn requirements into questions.
pages.lead: A concept matrix can record an intention, the missing evidence and the type of responsible reviewer needed. It should not show unperformed tests as passed.
pages.body: Example: intended clarity; evidence unknown; source to seek a suitable real evaluation. This is a question record, not a compliance or engineering checklist.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: Which requirement cannot be verified here?

pages.title: Separate the concept from validation.
pages.lead: The document supplies no prototype test, photometric result, electrical review or manufacturing analysis. A realistic illustration does not replace those activities.
pages.body: Do not operate equipment, build an electrical device or infer safe instructions from this template. Appropriate specialist work would be separate from the visual concept.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: What must a qualified real process evaluate?

pages.title: Prepare a source-aware handoff.
pages.lead: Share the intended visual direction, retained alternative and unresolved evidence together. The next reader should not have to guess which claims remain assumptions.
pages.body: A concept handoff is not permission to manufacture, procure or operate a product. No approval, certification or supplier commitment is supplied.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: Which phrase prevents a premature production claim?

pages.title: Keep the next design question open.
pages.lead: Close with the question that would most improve the design brief if appropriately investigated. Do not imply that the object is ready for sale or use.
pages.body: All five illustrations are visual references; repeated placements do not increase their count. The native document remains editable without turning its assumptions into evidence.
